description: A clean two-record pass whose subject is ORDER rather than content, and the only case in this directory that can fail on ordering alone. app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl displays every record twice - once at L96, inside the '00' arm of 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT, and again at L78 in the mainline - and both displays happen within ONE iteration of the PERFORM UNTIL END-OF-FILE = 'Y' loop at L74-81, before the next READ is issued. The two lines belonging to a record are therefore ADJACENT, so the expected sequence is the L71 banner, row 1, row 1, row 2, row 2, the L85 banner. The misreading this case exists to catch is that the file is displayed once per record inside the read paragraph and then replayed at the end, which would give the L71 banner, row 1, row 2, row 1, row 2, the L85 banner. Those two orderings hold the IDENTICAL multiset of lines and differ only in sequence, so a comparison that sorted or set-ified the messages would pass both; FieldDiffer compares expectedMessages position by position, which is what makes this case mean anything. The third READ reports '10', which moves 16 into APPL-RESULT, satisfies APPL-EOF and sets END-OF-FILE to 'Y' at L108 without displaying anything, and the CLOSE at L138 succeeds silently on '00', so nothing separates row 2's pair from the closing banner. Rows 0 and 1 of app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt are seeded verbatim in ascending key order, 000000001 then 000000002, and each is pinned across all 19 CVCUS01Y spans rather than as an image, because naming the spans makes the field names themselves part of the assertion: CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD is among them, and app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy declares the same 10-byte span at the same offset under a different name that the statement package models separately, so a translation which collapsed the two layouts onto one type is reported as a missing field rather than passing silently (requirement I1). CUSTFILE is opened INPUT and the program issues no WRITE and no REWRITE, so expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion and the final state is the pre-state, read back from the relation rather than echoed from the seed. app/jcl/READCUST.jcl:L6 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBCUS01C with no PARM, so no job parameter is declared, and GOBACK at L87 never touches RETURN-CODE, so the run ends at 0 and no abend site is reached. Driven through CustomerFileReaderJob's tasklet with CustomerService holding the decisions - no HTTP layer and no JobLauncher in the path. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED, by structured reading of the COBOL paragraphs cross-checked against the CVCUS01Y byte layout, the READCUST.jcl DD contract and the real shipped app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture; none of it was captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment (AAP 0.7.6, risk R-A).
